```lean
MeasureTheory.snorm.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup F] :
  {x : MeasurableSpace α} → (α → F) → ℝ≥0∞ → Measure α → ℝ≥0∞
```
***
`ℒp` seminorm, equal to `0` for `p=0`, to `(∫ ‖f a‖^p ∂μ) ^ (1/p)` for `0 < p < ∞` and to
`essSup ‖f‖ μ` for `p = ∞`. 
***
*import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic*

```lean
MeasureTheory.snorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_nnnorm.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_3} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  {p : ℝ≥0∞} {μ : Measure α} [NormedAddCommGroup F] (hp_ne_zero : p ≠ 0) (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤) {f : α → F} :
  snorm f p μ = (∫⁻ (x : α), ↑‖f x‖₊ ^ p.toReal ∂μ) ^ (1 / p.toReal)
```
***
*import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic*

```lean
MeasureTheory.mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
  (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (ε : ℝ≥0∞) : ε * μ {x | ε ≤ f x} ≤ ∫⁻ (a : α), f a ∂μ
```
***
**Markov's inequality** also known as **Chebyshev's first inequality**. 
***
*import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue*

```lean
  {β : Type u_5} [SeminormedAddCommGroup β] {f : α → β} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
  AEMeasurable (fun a => ↑‖f a‖₊) μ
```
***
*import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Basic*

```lean
AEMeasurable.pow_const.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {α : Type u_4} [MeasurableSpace β]
  [MeasurableSpace γ] [Pow β γ] [MeasurablePow β γ] {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} {f : α → β}
  (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) (c : γ) : AEMeasurable (fun x => f x ^ c) μ
```
***
*import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.Arithmetic*

```lean
MeasureTheory.pow_mul_meas_ge_le_snorm.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] {p : ℝ≥0∞} (μ : Measure α) {f : α → E} (hp_ne_zero : p ≠ 0) (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤)
  (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (ε : ℝ≥0∞) : (ε * μ {x | ε ≤ ↑‖f x‖₊ ^ p.toReal}) ^ (1 / p.toReal) ≤ snorm f p μ
```

```lean
dite.{u} {α : Sort u} (c : Prop) [h : Decidable c] (t : c → α) (e : ¬c → α) : α
```
***
"Dependent" if-then-else, normally written via the notation `if h : c then t(h) else e(h)`,
is sugar for `dite c (fun h => t(h)) (fun h => e(h))`, and it is the same as
`if c then t else e` except that `t` is allowed to depend on a proof `h : c`,
and `e` can depend on `h : ¬c`. (Both branches use the same name for the hypothesis,
even though it has different types in the two cases.)

We use this to be able to communicate the if-then-else condition to the branches.
For example, `Array.get arr ⟨i, h⟩` expects a proof `h : i < arr.size` in order to
avoid a bounds check, so you can write `if h : i < arr.size then arr.get ⟨i, h⟩ else ...`
to avoid the bounds check inside the if branch. (Of course in this case we have only
lifted the check into an explicit `if`, but we could also use this proof multiple times
or derive `i < arr.size` from some other proposition that we are checking in the `if`.)
